rv.q: But apart from the creative production values, there is not a lot of substance to the play...
It's a study of ambiguity that becomes a master class in obfuscation.
By the end of this long one act play, you may be less confused but then again you might be just as at sea as at the beginning.
Indeed, it’s flabbergasting how hard the production works at self-sabotage.

I know it was intended for the artists, but it could just as well have been for those of us who sat politely throughout its 80 minutes of sheer dramaturgic and directorial malpractice without sneaking out for an early trip home.
The Meeting: The Interpreter could impress you as ambitious and inventive—or it might wear you out if, instead, you find the stagecraft overblown and frenetic.
Frank Wood and Kelley Curran are terrific in the world premiere of The Meeting: The Interpreter. However, I'm completely flummoxed by the play.

cn.t: Critics find this Trump Tower meeting drama falls flat, with reviewers citing a lackluster exploration of its politically charged premise that fails to generate compelling theater from the infamous 2016 encounter.
